assertions.evidence: With both of the guest's notes pinned (setup so the pinned-note summary is populated) I edited note gnote_6295651c-23da-4df9-8f89-1779236f1a25 through the Edit control to 'contract-edited-b5 updated note body': the profile showed the new body (VAL-GUEST-016-profile-edited.png) and the Book detail sheet (?r=rsv_3d7d0e8b-...) showed it too (VAL-GUEST-016-book-summary-edited.png, detail-guest-pinned-notes = both pinned notes incl. the edited body). I then deleted the other note gnote_eec6f973-29ac-4b46-af2f-6531fe070159: the profile listed only the edited note (VAL-GUEST-016-profile-after-delete.png), and after two consecutive fresh loads of the Book sheet the summary showed only 'contract-edited-b5 updated note body' while the deleted text 'contract-pinned-b5' was absent from the whole page both times (VAL-GUEST-016-book-summary-after-delete.png). Network: PATCH .../notes/gnote_6295651c... -> 200 (edit), DELETE .../notes/gnote_eec6f973... -> 200. Read-only sqlite: the deleted row is a soft delete (deleted_at=1792240477712) and the edited row persists with body='contract-edited-b5 updated note body', pinned=1 (VAL-GUEST-005-015-016-db-evidence.txt); API GET .../guests/<id> returns notes=[edited note] and pinnedNotes=[edited note] with no deleted note, and GET /operator/reservations/book/reservations/<id> returns guest.pinnedNotes=[edited note] (VAL-GUEST-002-005-016-api-evidence.txt). Console errors: none.
assertions.notes: Both halves of the assertion were made observable in the Book summary by pinning the two notes first: the summary then shows the edited body and must not show the deleted one. The delete is a soft delete at the storage layer, which is exactly what keeps the deleted note from reappearing while visit/history data stays intact.
assertions.limitations: Pinning both notes before the edit/delete was an explicit setup step (the summary renders pinned notes only); it is recorded here rather than presented as part of the pass criteria.
